- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots in next 5–10 days; apply downward correction of 1–3% for 3–5 days post-spike.
- If sentiment turns positive after a downtrend, model frequently underreacts; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for 2–4 days following sentiment shift.
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 day horizons: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates when sentiment is volatile or mixed; cap forecast at 10% below recent 18-day high if sentiment is neutral or slightly negative.
- If sentiment is consistently positive (>0.2) over 5+ days, model tends to overforecast; apply 1–2% downward adjustment for 5–7 days ahead.
